 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Alok Kumar Pandey
 Oral Order
3 21-02-2023 Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.P.P. for the State.

The present appeal has been filed against the judgment of conviction dated 30.09.2022 and order of sentence dated 13.10.2022 passed by learned Exclusive Special Judge (POCSO Act) cum 7th Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bhagalpur passed in connection with POCSO Case No.
24/2021 (arising out of Bihpur Jhandapur P.S. Case No. 62/2021, whereby the appellant has been convicted for the offences under Sections 376/511 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 8 of the POCSO Act and has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for five years and a fine of Rs.10,000/- under Sections 376/511 of the I.P.C. and in default of payment of fine, the appellant will have to suffer further simple imprisonment for six months.

entities.text: Exclusive Special Judge (POCSO Act) cum 7th Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bhagalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant has been further sentenced to undergo Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.4059 of 2022(3) dt.21-02-2023 rigorous imprisonment for five years and fine of Rs.10,000/- for the offence under Section 8 of the POCSO Act
and in default of payment of fine the appellant will have to suffer further simple imprisonment of six months.
Both sentences are directed to run concurrently.
As per prosecution case, allegation against the appellant is that he committed rape upon the informant's minor daughter.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is innocent and has committed no offence as alleged in the FIR and he has falsely been implicated in this case due to she-goat dispute.

He Bikesh Kumar Das @ Mukhiya @ Bikesh Ku Das vs The State Of Bihar on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120585973/
1 further submits that P.W.-1 to P.W.-6 are factual witnesses of the prosecution case and they have not supported prosecution case.

entities.text: Bikesh Kumar Das @ Mukhiya @ Bikesh Ku Das vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that P.W.-9 Dr. Anju Turiyar has stated that the victim has been examined and on the basis of supplementary report of the victim, spermatozoa has not found on vaginal swab examination.
He further submits that the appellant has got clean antecedent and he is in judicial custody since 15.02.2021 which is more than two years.
The appeal is not likely to be heard in near future.

Learned A.P.P. for the State vehemently opposed the prayer of bail of the appellant/convict and submits that Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.4059 of 2022(3) dt.21-02-2023 judgment is just and fair on the basis of evidence adduced by the prosecution witnesses.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as the period already undergone by the appellant which is more than two years, appeal is not likely to be heard in near future, argument advanced on behalf of both sides and also taking into consideration the material available on record,
let the appellant above-named be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- (twenty thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Exclusive Special Judge (POCSO Act) cum 7th Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bhagalpur passed in connection with POCSO Case No. 24/2021 (arising out of Bihpur Jhandapur P.S. Case No. 62/2021.
Sentence of the appellant is suspended and realization of fine shall also remain stayed during the pendency of the appeal.
The appellant is directed to cooperate this Court in disposal of the appeal.
(Alok Kumar Pandey, J) amitkumar/-
